title: Clinical practice guideline for the diagnosis of granulomatous-lymphocytic interstitial lung disease in patients with common variable immunodeficiency disorders: an ERS Clinical Research Collaboration.
abstract: Background Granulomatous-lymphocytic interstitial lung disease (GLILD) is a lung disease first described in people affected by common variable immunodeficiency disorders (CVID). Despite growing recognition of GLILD, there is no accepted diagnostic and management guideline, and current practice varies significantly across centres and countries. This clinical practice guideline provides evidence- and consensus-based recommendations on the screening and diagnosis of GLILD in patients with CVID. Methods A panel representing multiple interdisciplinary perspectives convened with methodologists to prioritise clinical questions, and review and assess the evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) methodology. Evidence-to-decision frameworks were used to decide on the direction and strength of recommendations. Results Screening for GLILD is recommended in all adult patients with CVID, preferably using high-resolution computed tomography. Evaluation should be performed by a multidisciplinary team. Routine lung biopsies are not mandatory but necessary for atypical presentations. As part of the diagnostic process, pulmonary infections should be excluded and lymphocytic alveolitis sought for by means of bronchoalveolar lavage. The severity of lung function impairment should be evaluated using pulmonary function tests including gas transfer assessment. Most of the recommendations are graded as conditional because of low certainty in the evidence regarding health effects. Conclusions This guideline allows for international homogeneity in the diagnosis of GLILD, thereby paving the way for improved comparability between centres, improving equity in healthcare for those affected by GLILD and facilitating multicentre research collaborations for future studies.

A panel representing multiple interdisciplinary perspectives convened with methodologists to prioritise clinical questions, and review and assess the evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) methodology. Evidence-to-decision frameworks were used to decide on the direction and strength of recommendations.

title: Left-sided 3D totally endoscopic mitral valve repair guided by left atrial appendage orientation in situs inversus totalis with mirror-image dextrocardia: a case report.
abstract: Background Situs inversus totalis with mirror-image dextrocardia is a rare anatomical condition that creates specific challenges for minimally invasive mitral valve surgery. In totally endoscopic procedures, the reversed cardiac orientation may affect thoracic access, peripheral cannulation, left atrial exposure and accurate identification of mitral valve segments. We report a case of left-sided three-dimensional totally endoscopic mitral valve repair in this setting, with emphasis on operative planning and intraoperative segment orientation. Case presentation A 39-year-old woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and New York Heart Association class II to III symptoms. Echocardiography showed severe mitral regurgitation caused by posterior leaflet prolapse involving P2 and extending toward P3. Computed tomography angiography confirmed situs inversus totalis, mirror-image dextrocardia, a right-sided aortic arch, bilateral superior vena cavae and an uninterrupted inferior vena cava. A left-sided three-dimensional totally endoscopic approach was used with peripheral cardiopulmonary bypass through the left femoral vessels and supplemental left internal jugular venous drainage. Intraoperative segment orientation was deliberately re-established using the left atrial appendage as a fixed landmark to identify the A1/P1 side and distinguish it from A3/P3. Valve repair consisted of neochordal implantation to the prolapsing posterior leaflet and ring annuloplasty. Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography, predischarge transthoracic echocardiography and 1-month follow-up transthoracic echocardiography showed no residual or recurrent mitral regurgitation, with preserved left ventricular systolic function at follow-up. Conclusions This case illustrates that valve-preserving, totally endoscopic mitral repair can be feasible in situs inversus totalis with mirror-image dextrocardia when imaging, cannulation, access and segment orientation are planned as a single operative strategy. The main educational message is that, in this case, the left atrial appendage served as a practical anatomical reference for maintaining segmental orientation during mitral repair in mirror-image anatomy.

title: Accuracy of 3D radiological skull measurements: reoriented sections and geometric correction versus caliper reference.
abstract: Purpose Three-dimensional radiological imaging is important for disease diagnosis and surgical planning, yet its accuracy in anatomical length measurements remains challenging. Standard sections calculations often underestimate actual dimensions due to orthographic projection distortions. This study evaluates the accuracy of reoriented section measurements and formula-based calculations compared to standard sections and reference caliper verifications. Methods A plastic human skull model was used for standardized length measurements. Five cranial dimensions (Ma-G, Ma-N, Ma-Rh, Ma-Ns, Ma-Me) were measured using a digital caliper as the reference. A computed tomography scan with a slice thickness of 0.625 mm was performed, and measurements were obtained from standard sections (sagittal, transverse, coronal), reoriented section, and formula-based calculations. Measurement agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis and repeated-measures ANOVA. Results Reoriented sections values (e.g., Ma-G: 13.18 ± 0.52 cm, Ma-N: 12.59 ± 0.24 cm) and formula-based calculations (e.g., Ma-G: 13.15 ± 0.26 cm, Ma-N: 12.61 ± 0.80 cm) closely matched caliper measurements (p > 0.05). In contrast, standard section parameters were significantly lower across all parameters (e.g., Ma-G sagittal: 12.03 ± 0.48 cm, p = 0.0005; coronal: 7.39 ± 0.56 cm, p < 0.0001). Bland-Altman analysis confirmed high agreement for reoriented sections and formula-based methods, whereas standard sections showed significant deviations (p < 0.05). Conclusion Reoriented sections findings and formula-based calculations offer accuracy comparable to caliper measurements, while standard sections results consistently underestimate the reference caliper values. These findings highlight the limitations of standard-section approaches and suggest that alternative methods may improve anatomical assessment in 3D imaging. These techniques may help reduce measurement-related discrepancies in settings requiring precise anatomical assessment. Such precision may be relevant in fields such as orthodontics, orthopedics, and implant planning, where accurate anatomical measurements are important.

title: Underlying thrombotic conditions in patients with splenic infarction: a 10-year retrospective analysis.
abstract: Background Splenic infarction is a rare but clinically important condition that is usually associated with underlying hematological, cardiovascular, infectious, or malignant diseases. Due to its nonspecific clinical presentation, diagnosis may be delayed. This study aimed to evaluate the demographic characteristics, clinical findings, etiological factors, radiological features, treatment approaches, and outcomes of patients diagnosed with non-traumatic splenic infarction. Methods This retrospective study included 67 adult patients diagnosed with splenic infarction by contrast-enhanced abdominal computed tomography (CT) at Dicle University Faculty of Medicine Hospital between January 2014 and December 2023. Demographic characteristics, presenting symptoms, laboratory parameters, radiological findings, etiological factors, treatment modalities, length of hospital stay, and in-hospital mortality were evaluated. Results The mean age of the patients was 50.9 ± 16.3 years, and 64.2% were male. Abdominal pain was the most common presenting symptom and was present in all patients. Hematological disorders were the most common identifiable specific etiology (31.3%), while no identifiable cause was found in 23.9% of patients. Contrast-enhanced CT established the diagnosis in all patients, whereas ultrasonography detected infarction in only 29.9% of cases. JAK2 mutation analysis was positive in 4 of 16 tested patients with hematological disorders. Conservative management was sufficient in 89.6% of patients, while 10.4% required splenectomy because of splenic rupture, hemorrhagic infarction, or splenic abscess formation. In-hospital mortality occurred in four patients (6.0%). Conclusions Splenic infarction is an uncommon clinical entity that should be considered in patients presenting with unexplained abdominal pain, particularly in the presence of hematological or systemic disorders associated with thrombotic risk. Contrast-enhanced CT remains the most reliable diagnostic modality, whereas ultrasonography has limited sensitivity. Although conservative management is effective in most patients, severe complications may necessitate surgical intervention. Early diagnosis and comprehensive etiological evaluation are essential for appropriate management and improved clinical outcomes. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Metastasis of lung carcinoma in a pheochromocytoma.
abstract: Tumor-to-tumor metastasis (TTM) is an established but rare entity. Lung carcinoma metastasizes commonly to adrenal glands; however, metastases into an already existing adrenal gland tumor are a rare finding. A 78-year-old man was diagnosed with pheochromocytoma, and during the disease staging, lung involvement was revealed. Functional imaging with both 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose ( 18 F-FDG) and 68 Ga-DOTA-Tyr3-Octreotate ( 68 Ga-DOTA-TATE) positron emission tomography (PET) was performed: 18 FDG-PET showed mild uptake in both the adrenal and pulmonary lesions, whereas 68 Ga-DOTA-TATE-PET revealed intense uptake confined to the adrenal mass. This discordant pattern suggested the presence of 2 biologically distinct lesions. The right adrenal gland was surgically removed, and histology and immunohistochemistry confirmed 2 components within the tumor: a pheochromocytoma that included a lung cancer metastasis. Histopathological confirmation of the pulmonary primary lesion was not available. This is the second published case of a TTM of lung carcinoma inside a pheochromocytoma. Tumor-to-tumor metastasis should be considered in pathological diagnosis.

title: Primary synovial sarcoma of the thyroid mimicking medullary thyroid cancer.
abstract: The differential diagnosis of a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass includes poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma, anaplastic carcinoma, medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), lymphoma, and metastatic disease. Although fine-needle aspiration (FNA) provides important diagnostic clues, it may not be definitive. We report a 43-year-old woman with a long-standing goiter that enlarged rapidly over 6 months. FNA suggested MTC; however, serum calcitonin and carcinoembryonic antigen levels were within normal limits, creating clinicobiochemical discordance. Given this discrepancy, further evaluation was undertaken. Core needle biopsy of the thyroid mass demonstrated a spindle cell neoplasm, and immunohistochemistry supported a diagnosis of primary synovial sarcoma. Gallium-68-labeled 1,4,7,10-tetraazacyclododecane-1,4,7,10-tetraacetic acid-octreotate positron emission tomography-computed tomography revealed distant metastases involving the lungs, bones, and bone marrow. In view of advanced disease with vascular encasement and metastatic spread, neoadjuvant chemotherapy was initiated. This case highlights the importance of histopathologic confirmation in atypical presentations of thyroid malignancy and underscores the limitations of cytology in rare spindle cell tumors.

title: Child Neurology: Transient Global Amnesia Precipitated by a Valsalva Maneuver in an Adolescent.
abstract: Transient global amnesia (TGA) is a benign clinical syndrome characterized by the sudden onset of anterograde amnesia with preserved consciousness and no focal neurologic deficits, resolving within 24 hours. It predominantly affects middle-aged and older adults and is rarely reported in pediatric populations. In adults, TGA is often preceded by identifiable triggers, including Valsalva maneuvers. We describe a previously healthy, typically developing 16-year-old boy who presented with acute anterograde amnesia after an intentional Valsalva maneuver performed during a school video. He experienced several hours of repetitive questioning, inability to form new memories, and mild retrograde amnesia. The episode of anterograde amnesia resolved spontaneously after approximately 9 hours. He subsequently regained some memories of the period preceding symptom onset. Neurologic examination after symptom resolution was normal aside from amnesia for the episode itself. Laboratory investigations, head CT, electroencephalography, and brain magnetic resonance imaging were unremarkable aside from a hypoplastic left transverse sinus without evidence of thrombosis. The clinical presentation was therefore felt to be most consistent with TGA precipitated by a Valsalva maneuvers. This case highlights a rare presentation of TGA in an adolescent precipitated by a Valsalva maneuver. It underscores the importance of considering TGA in the differential diagnosis of acute anterograde amnesia in pediatric patients and suggests overlap between recognized triggers of TGA in adults and those observed in children.

title: Tozuleristide Fluorescence-Guided Resection of Gliomas: Results of a Phase II Investigator-Initiated Study.
abstract: Background and objectives This Phase II, investigator-initiated, nonrandomized clinical trial evaluated tozuleristide, a tumor-specific near-infrared fluorescence imaging agent, combined with the Canvas® imaging system (Blaze Bioscience) to enhance intraoperative visualization of glial tumors. Methods Subjects with newly diagnosed, suspected, biopsy-proven, or previously resected high- or low-grade central nervous system tumors received 24 mg (contrast-enhancing glioma) or 36 mg (non-contrast-enhancing glioma) of tozuleristide 1 to 24 hours before surgery. Tumors were visualized intraoperatively using the Canvas imaging system. Biopsies were collected to assess tozuleristide sensitivity and specificity by comparing with histopathology assessment. Extent of resection (EOR), calculated from preoperative and postoperative MRI, was compared with historical controls. Fluorescence did not guide resection, and subjects were not selected for maximal EOR. Results Thirty-nine subjects (33 contrast-enhancing, 6 nonenhancing tumors) underwent all study procedures. Fluorescence was observed in 30/33 contrast-enhancing tumors. Across 191 biopsies, fluorescence showed sensitivity = 0.735, specificity = 0.500, positive predictive value (PPV) = 0.847, negative predictive value = 0.333, and accuracy = 0.685. Residual fluorescence occurred only when total resection was unsafe and showed a nonsignificant negative correlation with EOR (r = -0.318). The mean EOR was 90.09% (24 mg tozuleristide) with 12 subjects achieving gross-total resection; 0/6 nonenhancing tumors fluoresced. Among patients with glioblastoma undergoing repeat resection, exploratory comparison with historical controls showed higher gross-total resection rates in tozuleristide-treated subjects (6/11 vs 2/11, P = .076); however, fluorescence was not incorporated into surgical decision-making, and these results thus cannot be interpreted toward efficacy. Conclusion Tozuleristide demonstrated tumor-specific fluorescence with high sensitivity and PPV at 24 mg. The high PPV suggests that fluorescence may be useful for confirming tumor presence in enhancing gliomas, but the low negative predictive value seen cannot exclude tumor in the absence of fluorescence, particularly in infiltrative margins. A well-controlled Phase III trial is necessary to determine the efficacy of image-guided resection in improving EOR.

title: Lateral Mass Fusion Using 3D-Printed Anatomic Cages for Atlantoaxial Dislocation: A Multicenter Comparison With Iliac Crest Autograft.
abstract: Background and objectives Atlantoaxial dislocation (AAD) is a high-risk condition that can lead to significant mortality. Lateral mass fusion offers structural stability and reduction, yet no standardized fusion device currently exists for consistent atlantoaxial fixation. This study compares the clinical outcomes of a novel anatomic cage vs iliac crest autograft in treating AAD. Methods Radiographic, laboratory, and clinical outcomes were retrospectively compared between 2 surgical groups: one treated with an iliac crest autograft by a traditional posterior approach, the other treated with an anatomic cage using an intermuscular approach. Health-related quality-of-life factors were also analyzed. Results One hundred nineteen patients underwent fusion with iliac crest autograft and 105 with anatomic cages were finally included. The iliac crest group had a shorter operative time ( P = .043), but the anatomic cage group had significantly less intraoperative blood loss, shorter hospitalization, and fewer C2 neurological symptoms (all P < .05). Bony fusion was similar between 2 groups (3.3 [0.6] months vs 3.1 [0.4] months, P = .163). Compared with the iliac crest group, the anatomic cage group showed greater improvements in lateral mass interspace height (LMIH, P < .001). Inflammatory markers were significantly lower at postoperative day 3 in the anatomic cage group. Improvement in pain (Visual Analog Scale) differed significantly between groups (Δ P <.001). Regression analysis showed that age <55 years was independently associated with greater Neck Disability Index improvement ( P = .025), while C1-C2 Cobb angle and cervicomedullary angle correlated with postoperative Japanese Orthopaedic Association and Neck Disability Index scores. LMIH was significantly associated with C2 neurological symptoms ( P = .015). Conclusion Lateral mass fusion using the 3-dimensional-printed anatomic cages by an intermuscular approach is a safe and effective treatment of AAD. It offers improved radiological outcomes, preserves C2 nerve root integrity, and reduces early postoperative inflammation. In addition, intraoperative restoration of LMIH may reduce neurological symptoms in patients with AAD.

title: Delta 68 Ga-Pentixafor PET/CT Radiomics Models for the Detection of Surgically Curable Primary Aldosteronism.
abstract: Objective Unilateral primary aldosteronism (PA) can be cured through adrenalectomy. We developed a 68 Ga-Pentixafor positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) radiomics model to detect surgically curable PA. Methods A total of 359 patients with PA who underwent dual-time-phase (10 min and 40 min) 68 Ga-Pentixafor PET/CT were enrolled from two centers (center 1 = 268; center 2 = 91). Radiomics models were developed based on 10-min PET, 40-min PET, and delta PET features. The performance of the three PET models and the combined clinical-radiomics model was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves. Model accuracy and clinical utility were assessed with calibration curves and decision curve analysis. Results Among the eight radiomics models, the XGBoost model achieved the best classification performance and was selected for the final model. Among the three PET models, the delta PET model yielded the highest area under the curve in the training set (0.875; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.814-0.935), validation set (0.861; 95% CI 0.754-0.968), and external test set (0.860; 95% CI 0.773-0.946). The combined clinical-radiomics model showed superior area under the curve values: 0.926 (95% CI 0.891-0.962) in training, 0.909 (95% CI 0.836-0.983) in validation, and 0.919 (95% CI 0.855-0.982) in external testing. The combined model outperformed the PET/CT model across all datasets and demonstrated good calibration and clinical utility. Conclusion The model incorporating delta 68 Ga-Pentixafor PET/CT radiomics features and clinical features optimizes the selection of patients with surgically curable PA, providing reliable decision support for precision surgical treatment.

title: Artificial intelligence for women's reproductive health: A scoping review of global diagnostic trends, methodological gaps, and a translational research agenda for low-resource settings.
abstract: Women's reproductive and endocrine disorders including Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), endometriosis, thyroid disorders, infertility, and pregnancy-related complications remain a major global health burden. These conditions are especially difficult to manage in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where diagnostic facilities and specialist care are limited. We conducted a PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) applications in women's reproductive and hormonal health. Our search covered five databases PubMed, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science, and Google Scholar and included peer-reviewed studies published between 2021 and 2025. A total of 116 eligible studies were identified and classified into six categories: clinical prediction and risk modeling, medical imaging and AI, biomarker discovery and multi-omics, reproductive and endocrine health applications, clinical decision support systems, and AI/ML methodology development. Ensemble methods such as Random Forest and Gradient Boosting showed strong and consistent diagnostic performance. Convolutional neural networks performed well in single-centre settings but showed reduced performance upon external validation, consistent with optimism bias. Overall, 83.6% of studies were classified as high risk of bias and 75.5% lacked external validation. After adjusting for population size, high-income countries produced 23 times more studies per million women of reproductive age than LMICs. Sub-Saharan Africa contributed fewer than 0.1 studies per million women, and no studies were identified from Nepal or Sri Lanka. Current evidence, which is heavily concentrated in high-income and East Asian settings, is insufficient to support population-level deployment. We introduce a four-tier LMIC feasibility classification system that links data modality, infrastructure requirements, and personnel needs. We also propose a phased research agenda that separates near-term priorities (0-2 years) from medium-term goals that depend on infrastructure investment.

title: Development and evaluation of a deep incremental learning system for mammography image analysis.
abstract: Introduction Breast cancer is a malignant tumor that mostly stems from ductal or lobular epithelial tissues. Each year, over two million people suffer from this disease and over half a million pass away globally, ranking breast cancer the most prevalent cancer type in women and the second cause of cancer-related deaths. Periodic screening programs such as mammography have significantly improved survival via early detection. Therefore, facilitating the interpretation for this modality through Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) systems can accelerate specialists' decision-making and further raise the survival rates. Materials and methods A CAD web-based system was designed through Unified Modeling Language (UML) according to the three-tier architecture. The design was implemented using C# programming language and the ASP.NET 8 framework along with the Microsoft Structured Query Language (MSSQL) database. The ViTGEMC deep ensemble model with Incremental Learning (IL) capabilities was incorporated as the prediction engine. Moreover, the system evaluation was conducted in two phases: a multi-reader and multi-case experiment to appraise the system's assistance effect, and the user experience assessment via the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ). Results The impact of software predictions was evaluated in an interventional test with the participation of four radiology specialists and 40 dual-view examinations, which yielded a 19.5% reduction in interpretation time (404.9 ± 104.2 vs. 325.8 ± 80.3 seconds, p = 0.0203) while maintaining accuracy (0.769 ± 0.024 vs. 0.800 ± 0.147, p = 0.6560). The usability assessment was further conducted by 10 experts in medicine, radiology, and health information technology fields, in which the system achieved scores of 1.4 to 2.3 across the six UEQ aspects of user experience. Conclusion The CAD software provides a convenient and enhanced environment which can aid radiologists in quicker diagnosis.

title: Age at dementia diagnosis, subtype associations, and neuroimaging differentiation in Bangladesh: The CARED study.
abstract: Background Evidence on age at diagnosis of dementia and differentiation of dementia subtypes in Bangladesh is limited. This study aimed to determine age at diagnosis, examine factors associated with dementia subtypes, and evaluate the discriminatory utility of neuroimaging scales in a Bangladeshi clinical population. Methods The Community Awareness and Research on Early Dementia (CARED) study was a cross-sectional observational study conducted 2019-2024 at a tertiary care centre in Bangladesh. A total of 658 adults presenting with cognitive impairment, undergoing evaluation for suspected dementia were included. Diagnoses were established using DSM-5 criteria by a multidisciplinary team. Patients were categorized into dementia subtypes. Pseudodementia was retained as separate comparator group. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with dementia subtypes. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analyses were used to assess the discriminatory performance of neuroimaging scales. Results Among 658 patients, Alzheimer's-related dementia (ARD) accounted for 51.7% of cases. The mean age at diagnosis was significantly higher in ARD compared with non-Alzheimer's-related dementia (nARD) (67.7 ± 10.8 vs 64.3 ± 11.4 years, P < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, nARD was associated with an earlier age at diagnosis by 4.3 years compared with ARD. Vascular dementia was associated with hypertension, OR 4.2 (95% CI 1.1-16.6), P = 0.04, and smoking, OR 13.1 (95% CI 1.6-103.3), P = 0.01. Neuroimaging scales demonstrated variable discriminatory performance. Medial temporal atrophy showed good discrimination for ARD (AUROC 0.752), while Fazekas scores demonstrated good performance for vascular dementia (AUROC 0.838) and mixed dementia (AUROC 0.836). Global cortical atrophy showed moderate discriminatory ability for frontotemporal dementia (AUROC 0.659). Conclusions Age at diagnosis varied across dementia subtypes in this Bangladeshi clinical cohort, with non-Alzheimer's diagnosed earlier than Alzheimer's. Structured MRI visual rating scales showed variable subtype-specific discriminatory performance, suggesting that they may provide adjunctive information for dementia subtype differentiation when interpreted alongside multidisciplinary clinical assessment.

title: The Use of Gadoxetic Acid-Enhanced MRI as a Diagnostic Tool in Cases of Biliary Atresia: A Two-Case Report.
abstract: Early diagnosis of biliary atresia (BA) remains challenging, although timely recognition is critical for achieving favorable surgical outcomes. We present two infants in whom gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI demonstrated imaging findings that supported early suspicion of BA. Two neonates with persistent cholestasis underwent routine laboratory evaluation, targeted ultrasonography, and hepatocyte-specific magnetic resonance imaging using gadoxetic acid. This contrast agent is actively taken up by functioning hepatocytes and is normally excreted into the biliary system during the delayed hepatobiliary phase, allowing functional assessment of bile formation and excretion. MRI findings, particularly biliary excretion on delayed images, were evaluated and correlated with intraoperative cholangiography. In both infants, hepatic parenchymal enhancement after contrast administration was preserved, indicating intact hepatocellular uptake. However, no biliary excretion was observed on delayed hepatobiliary-phase images. Intraoperative cholangiography confirmed biliary atresia in both cases. Although the diagnosis of biliary atresia is traditionally based on clinical findings, laboratory parameters, and ultrasonography, these approaches may remain inconclusive in some patients. Our findings suggest that gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI, by demonstrating preserved hepatocellular uptake with absent biliary excretion, may serve as a useful adjunctive diagnostic tool and contribute to earlier and more confident identification of biliary atresia.

title: WHICH FACTORS CAN DEFINE THE PROGNOSIS OF ARTICULAR FRACTURES OF THE CAPITELLUM AND TROCHLEA?
abstract: Introduction Articular fractures of the distal humerus involving the capitellum and trochlea (AO 13B3) are complex and challenging to manage without consensus in the literature on the most appropriate management. Objective Evaluate radiographic features and treatment-related factors that may be positively or negatively correlated with the outcome of these fractures. Methods Sixteen adult patients who underwent surgery between 2007 and 2024 with at least one year of follow-up were analyzed retrospectively. Radiographic characteristics, postoperative range of motion, and complications were evaluated. Statistical analysis used Odds Ratio (OR) and Fisher's Exact Test. Results Elbow stiffness occurred in 56% of patients, 83% of which were in cases with posterior wall involvement (OR=7.5; p=0.08). Preoperative immobilization for more than seven days was associated with range of motion impairment (60%, OR=3; p=0.58) and ulnar nerve neuropathy (30%, OR=6; p=0.09). All cases of ulnar neuropathy occurred in women with prolonged immobilization (OR=8.08; p=0.09). Conclusion Posterior wall integrity is a relevant prognostic factor for the final range of motion. The propensity for ulnar neuropathy in women and those with prolonged immobilization, although without statistical significance, suggests the need for larger samples. Level of Evidence II; Retrospective study.

title: AT(N)-Anchored Multimodal Deep Learning for Alzheimer’s Staging: A Taxonomy and Continuous Burden Index for Low-Resource Settings
abstract: The global burden of dementia is heavily concentrated in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet biological diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) relies on positron emission tomography (PET) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis that are operationally inaccessible in these regions. The 2024 Alzheimer’s Association revised criteria recognize sufficiently accurate plasma assays,particularly p-tau217,as Core 1 biomarkers that may support biological diagnosis, offering a scientifically credible pathway to infrastructure-light biological detection and staging. However, the machine learning literature has expanded without principled mapping to the AT(N) biological framework or rigorous consideration of deployability constraints in resource limited settings. We present a systematic scoping review synthesizing 146 included full-text publications (2018–2026) across four multidisciplinary evidence streams, establishing a novel architectural taxonomy that maps deep learning architectural families directly to AT(N) biological targets and connects model inductive biases to specific biomarker categories. We audit major AD datasets, identify critical biases in demographic and biomarker representation, and map pervasive data pathologies—label scarcity, missing modalities, scanner heterogeneity, and population bias—to corresponding ML/DL remediation strategies. Finally, we argue for a shift from binary classification toward continuous, biologically anchored disease-burden scoring, proposing the Alzheimer’s Disease Burden Index (ADBI). The ADBI equations presented herein represent a theoretical and architectural framework designed to guide future prospective validation on multi-ethnic cohorts. This work provides a methodological roadmap for developing globally deployable, equity aware AD diagnostic models.

title: An Extra-gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor Masquerading as an Adrenal Mass: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Background: Extra-gastrointestinal stromal tumors (EGISTs) are rare mesenchymal neoplasms arising outside the gastrointestinal tract, most often in the omentum, mesentery, or retroperitoneum. Presentation as a suprarenal mass mimicking primary adrenal pathology is exceedingly uncommon, with only isolated cases reported in the literature. We describe the clinical course, diagnostic evaluation, surgical management, and pathological findings of a retroperitoneal EGIST that was preoperatively presumed an adrenocortical carcinoma. Case Presentation: A 74-year-old woman presented with left flank pain. Computed tomography (CT) imaging demonstrated a 5.8 x 6.1 x 4.9 cm heterogeneous left suprarenal mass with central necrosis, raising concern for adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC), pheochromocytoma, or metastatic disease. Comprehensive hormonal evaluation was negative. CT of the chest confirmed no metastatic disease. The patient underwent robot-assisted retroperitoneal laparoscopic left adrenalectomy with periaortic lymph node dissection. Final pathology revealed a low-grade GIST (spindle cell type, 7.5 cm, CD117+) arising from retroperitoneal soft tissue with the adrenal gland identified as a separate, uninvolved structure. Staging: pT3N0M0R1 (0/4 lymph nodes positive). The patient was discharged on postoperative day 2 without complications. Conclusion: GIST should be included in the differential of large retroperitoneal suprarenal masses. Immunohistochemistry — particularly CD117 (c-Kit) — is essential for definitive diagnosis. KIT/PDGFRA mutational analysis is mandatory to guide adjuvant tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy. Multidisciplinary oncologic review is warranted given the R1 resection and paucity of outcome data for retroperitoneal EGISTs.

title: Alveolar Bone Mineral Density Correlates with Lumbar Spine Bone Mineral Density During Romosozumab Therapy: A Prospective Observational Study In Osteoporosis
abstract: Abstract Early osteoporosis detection remains challenging because of the limited accessibility of dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), sparking interest in the use of routine dental radiographs to assess alveolar bone mineral density (al-BMD). This prospective observational study evaluated the longitudinal changes in al-BMD during osteoporosis therapy, its association with systemic BMD and its utility as a screening and monitoring tool in female patients. al-BMD was quantified using standardized intraoral radiographs with reference phantoms, while systemic BMD and bone turnover markers were concurrently monitored. At baseline, al-BMD was significantly lower in patients with untreated osteoporosis than in both young and elderly non-osteoporotic controls. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated high diagnostic performance for al-BMD in identifying untreated osteoporosis, showing a positive correlation with the lumbar spine BMD but not with the femoral neck BMD and the total hip BMD. During sequential bone-anabolic therapy, al-BMD significantly increased over time, eventually reaching levels comparable to those of elderly non-osteoporotic controls. Also, al-BMD changes like those observed in systematic BMD. These findings suggest that al-BMD derived from dental radiographs is a clinically promising adjunct for osteoporosis screening and monitoring treatment-associated bone improvements.

title: Prenatal Diagnosis and Genetic Etiology of Fetal Polycystic Kidney Disease: A Single-Center Retrospective Study of 147 Cases in Yunnan Province, Southwest China
abstract: Abstract Background Fetal polycystic kidney disease (FPDK) is a common ultrasound finding, but its genetic causes vary widely, and data from Yunnan Province are scarce. We aimed to fill this gap by systematically testing a large local cohort. Methods We reviewed 147 FPDK cases seen at our center in Yunnan between 2020 and 2024. All had karyotyping and CNV-seq as first-line tests. Families who tested negative on both were offered trio whole-exome sequencing (trio-WES). Outcomes came from medical records or phone calls. Results Karyotyping detected 18 chromosomal abnormalities (12.2%) mostly trisomy 21 (n = 10), trisomy 13 (n = 3), trisomy 18 (n = 1), 45,X (n = 1), and 47,XXY (n = 1) plus two structural rearrangements. CNV-seq identified isolated pathogenic CNVs in 14 cases (9.5%), ten of which (71.4%) were 17q12 deletions involving HNF1B. Among 32 families who went on to trio-WES, we identified diagnostic single gene variants in 19 (59.4% of those tested, 12.9% overall). The main culprits were PKD1 (n = 6), PKHD1 (n = 4), BBS2 (n = 2), and one each of BBS7 , TMEM67 , TMEM237 , NEK8 , VHL , HNF1B , HDAC8 , CELSR1 , BUB1B , and GRIN1 . All told, we found a genetic cause in 51 of 147 cases (34.7%). Of these, 44 families (86.3%) chose to terminate. Conclusions In this Yunnan cohort, trisomy 21, 17q12 deletion, and PKHD1 / PKD1 mutations were the leading causes. A two-step approach parallel karyotyping and CNV-seq first, then trio-WES for negatives greatly improves detection and gives families essential information for decision‑making. These results offer much needed regional data for prenatal counseling in Yunnan and surrounding areas.

title: Risk Factors for Cervical Lymph Node Metastasis and a Predictive Model for Lateral Cervical Lymph Node Metastasis in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma
abstract: Abstract Background: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) is the most common thyroid malignancy. Although the overall prognosis is favorable, cervical lymph node metastasis (LNM) occurs in a substantial proportion of patients and affects both surgical planning and clinical outcomes. Preoperative ultrasonography remains limited in sensitivity, particularly for occult metastases, and existing predictive tools rarely distinguish between central and lateral compartments. A dedicated model for lateral cervical lymph node metastasis (LC-LNM) is therefore needed. Methods: This single-center retrospective study enrolled 450 patients with newly diagnosed PTC who underwent thyroid surgery between January 2022 and December 2024. Clinicopathological characteristics, BRAF V600E mutation status, preoperative ultrasound features, and surgical data were collected. Variables associated with central lymph node metastasis (CLNM) and LC-LNM were identified by univariate analysis and entered into multivariable binary logistic regression. Model performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, Hosmer–Lemeshow goodness-of-fit testing, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Results: Tumor maximum diameter, BRAF V600E mutation, calcification, and male sex were significantly associated with CLNM. For LC-LNM, tumor diameter, BRAF V600E mutation, calcification, a taller-than-wide shape (aspect ratio >1), tumor laterality (unilateral vs. bilateral), and an indistinct tumor margin were identified as independent correlates. In the resulting LC-LNM model, tumor diameter, BRAF V600E mutation, calcification, and aspect ratio >1 were positive predictors, whereas unilateral lesions and a clear tumor margin were negative predictors. The model showed good fit (Hosmer–Lemeshow P = 0.526) and an AUC of 0.863. Calibration was high (MAE = 0.016; MSE < 0.001; 90th percentile absolute error = 0.055), and DCA indicated net clinical benefit across a threshold probability range of 0.05–0.65. Conclusion: LNM in PTC is associated with a distinct set of clinicopathological factors in the central and lateral compartments. The proposed LC-LNM model integrates readily available preoperative clinical, ultrasound, and molecular variables and may serve as a quantitative adjunct to guide individualized decision-making regarding lateral neck dissection.

title: Functional Transopercular Transinsular Mesialtemporal Surgical Corridor in Mesial Temporal-Insular Tumors
abstract: Abstract Background Transcortical approaches to insula tumours have gained popularity in the recent years alongside with the widespread use of awake surgical techniques and intraoperative neuromonitoring developments. The transopercular transinsular mesialtemporal surgical corridor offers a functional approach for accessing mesial temporal-insular lesions. Case presentations and Surgical technique: A 36-year-old woman who presented with epileptic seizures and was found to have a left temporo-insular lesion on MRI. The technique performed through the temporal opercula after cortical mapping for the relevant cognitive functions – language, cognition and motor. Preoperative cortical mapping with navigated transcranial magnetic stimulation and/or functional MRI provide significant preoperative information to inform intraoperative cortical mapping. After skeletonizing the M3 branches, the approach follows a surgical structural corridor between arcuate fasciculus, superior longitudinal fasciculus system, fronto-aslant tract, and corticospinal tract superiorly and medially, inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus medially, uncinate fasciculus anteriorly, inferior and medial longitudinal fasciculus laterally and optic radiations posteriorly, reaching the mesial temporal region – uncus and hippocampal formation. At subcortical level, the boundaries of this structural corridor are functionally identified with the appropriate intraoperative testing. Asleep intraoperative testing focuses on motor evoked potentials (MEPs) mapping and monitoring using either high frequency (HFS) or low frequency (LFS) techniques, somatosensory evoked potentials (SSEPs) and/or cortico-cortical evoked potentials (CCEP). Awake intraoperative mapping and monitoring relies on the above mentioned techniques and temporary cognitive function disruption using language, social and motor cognition tasks - with either HFS or LFS techniques. Conclusion The functional transopercular transinsular mesialtemporal surgical corridor enables maximal safe resection of tumors extending to the uncus and hippocampal formation while preserving functional cortical-subcortical structures and minimizing vascular morbidity.

title: Prevalence and Associated Factors of Low Bone Mass Among 937 Nursing Staff at a Tertiary Hospital in China: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Abstract Background Nursing staff face multiple occupational risk factors for bone health deterioration, yet large-scale epidemiological data on bone mineral density (BMD) in this population remain limited. This study, embedded within an ongoing occupational health cohort of nurses established in 2021, aimed to investigate the prevalence of low bone mass and identify its independent risk factors among nursing staff. Methods A cross-sectional BMD sub-study was conducted in 2026 among 937 nursing staff at The First Hospital of Jilin University, China, as a follow-up wave of a nurses’ occupational health cohort initially enrolled in 2021 (n = 4,293). Forearm bone mineral density was assessed using quantitative ultrasound (BMD-A3, Pinyuan Medical, Jiangsu, China). Low bone mass was defined as a T-score < − 1.0. Data on demographics, lifestyle, reproductive factors, occupational factors, and nutritional habits were collected via questionnaire. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent risk factors. A prediction model was internally validated using ROC curve, calibration plot, and decision curve analysis. Results The prevalence of low bone mass was 21.7% (203/937), including 20.6% with osteopenia and 1.1% with osteoporosis. Multivariate logistic regression identified four independent factors: menopause (OR = 4.06, 95% CI 2.12–7.76, P < 0.001), history of falls (OR = 1.69, 95% CI 1.10–2.59, P = 0.016), sedentary behavior (OR = 1.53, 95% CI 1.10–2.13, P = 0.011), and history of fractures (OR = 0.33, 95% CI 0.13–0.86, P = 0.023). The model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.661 (95% CI 0.628–0.710), with good calibration (Hosmer–Lemeshow χ² = 4.81, P = 0.778) and net clinical benefit at threshold probabilities between 10% and 35%. Subgroup analyses confirmed the consistency of menopause across strata and showed amplified effects of sedentary behavior in overweight/obese individuals. Conclusions Menopause was the strongest risk factor for low bone mass, while sedentary behavior and falls were independent modifiable risk factors. Achieving recommended exercise levels did not fully offset the detrimental effects of prolonged sedentary behavior. These findings support workplace interventions targeting sedentary behavior reduction and BMD screening for peri-menopausal nursing staff.

title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance Pulmonary Artery Peak Flow Velocity as a Marker of Pulmonary Vascular Resistance in Fibrotic Interstitial Lung Disease
abstract: Abstract Background. Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a common and severe complication of interstitial lung disease (ILD), yet early diagnosis remains challenging. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) offers non-invasive assessment of pulmonary vascular hemodynamics, but evidence in PH associated with ILD is limited. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between CMR-derived parameters and invasive hemodynamics in patients with fibrotic ILD. Methods. In this prospective observational study, 41 patients with fibrotic ILD underwent pulmonary function testing, cardiopulmonary exercise testing, transthoracic echocardiography, and CMR. Twenty patients additionally underwent RHC. CMR-derived measurements included ventricular function parameters, heart chamber and great vessel dimensions, and pulmonary artery flow hemodynamic metrics. Associations between CMR parameters, invasive hemodynamics, exercise capacity and symptom burden were assessed using correlation, regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses. Results. Among 20 patients who underwent RHC, PH was confirmed in all cases, including 15 with isolated precapillary PH and 5 with combined PH. Pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) of over 5 Wood units defined severe PH in 6 patients who met the criteria. Pulmonary artery peak flow velocity (PA-Vmax) measured on CMR was significantly higher in the non-severe PH group (81.15 ± 19.27 cm/s vs. 52.33 ± 5.13 cm/s, p < 0.001) and demonstrated promising discriminatory performance for identifying severe PH (AUC 0.923, 95% CI 0.778-1.000, p = 0.004), with a threshold of < 62.5 cm/s yielding 100% sensitivity and 92.3% specificity. An inverse-transformed PA-Vmax model demonstrated a strong association with invasive PVR (R 2 = 0.651, F = 31.65, p < 0.001). Higher PA-Vmax correlated with greater exercise capacity, including higher anaerobic threshold (r = 0.419, p = 0.015) and maximal workload (r = 0.329, p = 0.050). Lower CMR-derived TAPSE was independently associated with greater dyspnea severity (β=-0.426, p = 0.025), while CMR-TAPSE/RHC-mPAP ratio demonstrated an even stronger association with symptom burden (r s =-0.570, p = 0.021). Conclusions. In patients with fibrotic ILD, CMR-derived PA-Vmax was significantly associated with PVR measured by RHC and demonstrated promising discrimination for severe PH in this exploratory cohort. CMR measurements of right ventricular adaptation were associated with functional capacity and dyspnea severity. These findings support further evaluation of CMR as a promising non-invasive modality for pulmonary vascular assessment in fibrotic ILD patients undergoing evaluation for suspected PH.

title: Subdural Empyema as the Presenting Feature of a Cerebral Aneurysm in a Pediatric Patient in the Intensive Care Unit of a Teaching Hospital in Maputo, Mozambique: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Cerebral aneurysms are rare in pediatric populations, accounting for less than 5% of all aneurysms. Etiologies are often congenital or infectious. To date, no cases of pediatric cerebral aneurysms have been reported in Mozambique. Case Presentation: We report the first documented case of a pediatric cerebral aneurysm in Mozambique. A 13-year-old boy was admitted to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) with a five-day history of sudden severe headache, fever, and right-sided focal seizures. Imaging revealed a right frontal parafalcine subdural empyema, which was surgically drained. Although the patient initially improved, he was readmitted 15 days later with a sudden loss of consciousness and generalized seizures. Encephalic Computed Tomography and angiography revealed intraventricular hemorrhage and ruptured aneurysms of the pericallosal and right middle cerebral arteries. Neurosurgical intervention was not available; The blood culture isolated Staphylococcus aureus , and broad-spectrum was considered, as well as supportive care, and the patient survived with neurological sequelae. Discussion This case highlights a rare and severe presentation of pediatric cerebral aneurysm associated with subdural empyema of likely infectious etiology. The vascular territories affected were atypical, and diagnosis was delayed due to the condition's rarity and limited resources. Conclusion Despite being rare, cerebral aneurysms in children should be considered in cases of neurological deterioration, especially with signs of intracranial infection. Early neuroimaging and timely neurosurgical care are essential for better outcomes in resource-limited settings.

title: Ultrasound-measured abdominal fat thickness: A diagnostic marker for metabolic syndrome and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in children and adolescents with obesity
abstract: Abstract Objective The increasing incidence of metabolic syndrome (MetS) and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) among children with obesity underscores the need to identify early, non-invasive biomarkers. Despite the extensive research on visceral fat, the predictive value of ultrasonographic subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) has received comparatively less attention. The present study evaluates the clinical utility of SAT as a diagnostic indicator in pediatric obesity. Methods The study prospectively evaluated children aged 7–18 years, including 61 obese patients and 41 controls. The diagnosis of MetS was made using modified WHO criteria. Abdominal Wall Fat Thickness (AWFT) was measured by a linear probe at the umbilical level, and hepatic steatosis was graded semi-quantitatively. The diagnostic accuracy was evaluated using ROC curves and logistic regression. Results This study demonstrated a significant correlation between AWFT and MetS as well as the severity of hepatic steatosis (p < 0.001). The optimal AWFT threshold for discriminating MetS was established at > 2.7 cm, which was associated with a 2.6-fold increased risk in the adjusted analysis (sensitivity: 75%, specificity: 66%, PPV: 60%, and NPV: 81%). Conclusion AWFT is a non-invasive, readily accessible ultrasonographic biomarker for MetS in children with obesity. Our findings suggest that incorporating an AWFT threshold of > 2.7 cm into routine pediatric obesity assessments could facilitate early identification of high-risk individuals and promote targeted intervention strategies.

title: Longitudinal Clinical and MRI Changes Suggestive of Subclinical Disease Progression in Egyptian Patients with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Prospective Observational Study
abstract: Abstract Background Progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA) is increasingly recognized as a major contributor to disability accumulation in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), reflecting ongoing neurodegeneration despite apparent control of inflammatory disease activity. However, longitudinal data integrating comprehensive clinical assessment with quantitative MRI biomarkers remain limited, particularly in North African populations. Methods This prospective observational cohort study included 50 patients with RRMS. Assessments at baseline, 6, and 12 months included the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS), Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT), Nine-Hole Peg Test (9-HPT), Timed 25-Foot Walk Test (T25-FWT), and Arabic Modified Fatigue Impact Scale (A-MFIS). Quantitative brain MRI, including regional volumetric analysis, cortical thickness measurements, and white matter lesion assessment, was performed at baseline and after one year. Results During the one-year follow-up, significant deterioration was observed in disability, cognitive performance, upper-limb function, and fatigue, whereas walking performance remained relatively stable. Clinically meaningful cognitive decline (≥ 4-point reduction in SDMT score) occurred in 24% of patients after 6 months and in 44% after one year. EDSS worsening was observed in eight patients at 6 months and seven patients at one year, including progression in 10.3% of patients without documented relapse during the second follow-up period. Quantitative MRI demonstrated significant longitudinal changes in multiple cortical and subcortical brain regions despite stable white matter lesion burden, and clinical deterioration was associated with regional brain volumetric alterations involving the thalamus, cortical and total gray matter, cerebellum, and temporal structures. Older age, longer disease duration, greater relapse burden, and delayed initiation of disease-modifying therapy (DMT) were associated with less favorable clinical outcomes and greater brain atrophy, whereas higher educational attainment and monosymptomatic disease onset were associated with better longitudinal cognitive performance. Conclusion One-year longitudinal follow-up demonstrated measurable changes across multiple clinical domains and regional brain structures consistent with early subclinical disease progression in RRMS despite limited inflammatory activity. Quantitative MRI combined with sensitive cognitive and functional assessments detected changes beyond those captured by conventional disability measures, supporting their complementary role in monitoring early neurodegenerative progression.

title: Single‑port endoscopic nipple-sparing mastectomy combined with prosthesis breast reconstruction in breast cancer: a retrospective single-center study of 167 cases
abstract: Abstract Background Single‑port endoscopic nipple-sparing mastectomy combined with prosthetic breast reconstruction (E-NSM-PBR) has been used for breast repair due to aesthetic considerations. However, the clinical feasibility, postoperative complications and oncological safety of E-NSM-PBR in breast surgery remain controversial. This study presents our experience with the application of E-NSM-PBR in breast cancer patients and reports the preliminary results. Methods This is a retrospective study of 167 patients who underwent breast surgery using E-NSM-PBR at our institution between March 1, 2023 and December 31, 2024. Their clinicopathological characteristics, postoperative complications, cosmetic outcomes, and oncologic outcomes were analyzed. Results All patients underwent nipple-sparing mastectomy under single-port endoscopy, followed by breast prosthesis reconstruction. The average duration of unilateral surgery is 222.9 minutes (ranging from 115 to 537 minutes). The average operation time on both sides was 371 minutes (ranging from 348 to 390 minutes). The average reconstruction volume was 253.6 ml (ranging from 100 to 445 ml). The overall complication rate was 16.8%. The subcutaneous fluid and infection in the breast area are the most common complications in breast reconstruction, with a total of 18 cases (10.2%). The combined necrosis rate of the nipple-areola complex (NAC) and skin flaps is 3.6%. There were 3 cases of implant loss after postoperative radiotherapy. The incidence of bleeding complications was the lowest, only 1.2%. Cosmetic outcomes were satisfactory in 94.6% of patients on a four-point scale by three-panel assessment and 95.8% using the BCCT.core software. After a median follow-up of 29 months, one local and one systemic recurrence were observed. Conclusions E-NSM-PBR is a safe and feasible immediate breast reconstruction technique with concealed surgical incision and promising oncologic safety. For suitable candidates, E-NSM-PBR technology can provide good cosmetic results.

title: Lightweight Deep Learning for Processing 3D Medical Images: A Systematic Review
abstract: Abstract Deep learning for three dimension (3D) modalities such as CT, MRI, and PET offers promise to improve diagnostic accuracy, surgical planning, and visualization of disease progression, as 3D image data provide high resolution volumetric representation. However, 3D deep learning models are computationally heavy and demand powerful hardware that is not always available or affordable, restrictingtheir use in resource-constrained settings such as rural clinics, edge devices, and low- and middle-income countries. Hence, there is a growing interest in building lightweight deep learning models, in general, and for 3D imaging, in particular. This article systematically and critically reviews lightweight deep learning for processing 3D medical images, examining model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation, quantization, pruning and efficient architectural designs, together with the datasets, tools, and deployment environments involved. These techniques substantially reduce parameters, memory, and inference time with modest accuracy loss. We also identify several research gaps in these approaches, such as the accuracy mismatch between lightweight and standard models, difficulty handling small anatomical structures while keeping models compact, limited testing on real resource-constrained hardware, weak integration of clinical information, and the absence of efficiency-aware evaluation metrics. We outline future directions, cluding robust lightweight designs, purpose-built compact 3D datasets, standardized efficiency metrics, and lightweight multimodal models.

title: Culler-Jones Syndrome Across Three Generations: Variable Expressivity of a Pathogenic GLI2 Variant—a Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Culler-Jones syndrome is a rare developmental disorder associated with pathogenic variants in GLI2 gene. The phenotype is highly variable and may include hypopituitarism, growth hormone deficiency, postaxial polydactyly, craniofacial abnormalities, and other developmental abnormalities involving midline structures. Variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance can complicate diagnosis and genetic counseling, particularly when relatives carrying the same pathogenic variant have few or no apparent manifestations. Case presentation A 24-year-old woman of Native American ancestry on both the maternal and paternal sides of her family was referred to the Adult Genetics Clinic for evaluation of congenital craniofacial abnormalities, hypopituitarism, growth hormone deficiency, short stature, and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Her history included bilateral cleft lip, anterior cleft palate, midline upper lip and gingival tissue masses, severe growth delay, and abnormal pubertal development. Brain magnetic resonance imaging performed in early childhood demonstrated a Chiari I malformation and absence of most or all of the pituitary gland. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous pathogenic variant in GLI2 , NM_005270.4:c.1421G>A (p.Trp474*). Targeted familial testing subsequently identified the same variant in her mother, sister, and maternal grandmother, all of whom were reportedly without significant manifestations of GLI2 -related disease. Her brother tested negative for the familial variant. The maternal family history was notable for postaxial polydactyly in multiple relatives. Two maternal uncles reportedly had both postaxial polydactyly and multiple supernumerary nipples, with up to five additional nipples reported in affected individuals. These relatives were not available to undergo genetic testing. Conclusions This family demonstrates marked variable expressivity associated with a pathogenic GLI2 variant across three generations. The proband had a severe multisystem phenotype, whereas three relatives carrying the same variant were reportedly without significant manifestations. Multiple supernumerary nipples in two maternal relatives who have not had molecular confirmation of the GLI2 familial variant represent a potentially new phenotype finding that has not been established as part of the recognized phenotype of Culler-Jones syndrome. This case highlights the importance of detailed family history assessment, cascade testing, and careful genetic counseling in families with GLI2 -related disease.

title: Canadian Preterm Brain Injury Consensus Classification for Cranial Ultrasound and Prediction of Neurodevelopmental Outcome in Preterm Infants
abstract: Abstract Objective To determine whether classification of severe preterm brain injury using the Canadian cranial ultrasound (cUS) consensus improves prediction of adverse neurodevelopmental outcomes. Study Design Infants born < 29 weeks’ gestation (2010–2018) with ≥ 3 cUS examinations, any brain injury, and neurodevelopmental assessment at 18–24 months were studied. Brain injury was assessed from serial cUS using the Canadian consensus classification. Severe injury comprised high-grade intraventricular hemorrhage, severe post-hemorrhagic ventricular dilatation, cystic white matter injury, and/or moderate-large cerebellar hemorrhage. Associations with death and/or significant neurodevelopmental impairment were analyzed and compared with historical reporting. Results Among 231 infants, 45% had severe brain injury and 39% experienced adverse outcome. Severe injury was independently associated with adverse outcome (OR 5.44, 95% CI 2.85–10.74). Sensitivity was similar to historical reporting, but specificity for cerebral palsy and severe cognitive delay was higher. Conclusions The Canadian cUS consensus classification improves neurodevelopmental outcome prediction and may inform early intervention and neuroprotective strategies.

title: Duality of Rarity of Chemotherapy-induced Flagellate Erythema among Cancer Patients: A Case Report with 26 Years of Evidence in Oncology.
abstract: Introduction Flagellate Dermatitis (FD) due to anticancer therapy is a rare, unusual Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) in oncology. The current case describes the impact of financial constraints on the choice of anticancer therapy, the occurrence of FD and poor outcomes among Hodgkin's Lymphoma patients, and 26 years of evidence on FD due to anticancer therapy. Case report A 25-year-old male presented with fever, cough, night sweats, weight loss, and swelling on the right side of the neck, which was diagnosed as Hodgkin's Lymphoma with a complex diagnostic work-up (PET-CT scan, histopathology/immunohistochemistry reports). The patient was planned for Nivolumab-AVD therapy, but treated with ABVD chemotherapy due to financial constraints. Unfortunately, the patient developed linear streaks on the trunk region of the body after 4 days of 1st dose of ABVD therapy, which was diagnosed as FD triggered by Bleomycin. Thus, Bleomycin was omitted from the polychemotherapy regimen (AVD), and ADR was managed with corticosteroids. Although the PET-CT report initially showed a partial response to ABVD/AVD. Later, the disease was found to be metabolically progressive, for which salvage therapy (GDP, DHAP, and palliative radiotherapy) was given. Further, the patient was suggested Brentuximab and Nivolumab therapy, but the patient declined therapy due to financial constraints, lack of funding, and coverage by the government healthcare scheme. Thus, the patient was discharged against medical advice. Conclusion Healthcare professionals should be aware of and vigilant for this whip-like dermatological manifestation (FD) when choosing Bleomycin-based therapy. A patient-centric approach to cessation or rechallenge with the culprit drug, along with antihistamines and topical/ oral corticosteroids, is the mainstay for the management of FD.

title: Surgical treatment of large vestibular schwannomas with hydrocephalus in octogenarians: Two cases with favorable functional outcomes.
abstract: Background The optimal management of vestibular schwannoma (VS) associated with hydrocephalus in octogenarians remains controversial. We report two patients aged 80 years or older with Koos grade IV VS who underwent surgical treatment. Case description Case 1 involved an 86-year-old woman who presented with progressive gait disturbance caused by a 3.5-cm cystic right VS associated with hydrocephalus. Case 2 involved an 81-year-old woman who presented with cognitive impairment and gait disturbance due to a 3.0-cm cystic left VS with hydrocephalus. In both patients, magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated narrowing of the high-convexity sulci, enlarged Sylvian fissures, and an acute callosal angle. Tumor resection was performed via a retrosigmoid approach with intraoperative facial motor evoked potential (FMEP) monitoring. Tumor dissection was terminated when FMEP amplitudes decreased to <50% of baseline values, resulting in subtotal or near-total tumor resection. Neither patient developed clinically significant postoperative facial nerve dysfunction. Both patients regained independent ambulation. Postoperative imaging demonstrated reduction of ventricular enlargement and improvement of hydrocephalus-related radiological findings. Cognitive function improved substantially in Case 2, with the Mini-Mental State Examination score increasing from 11 to 24. At the latest follow-up, the first patient remained independent without tumor progression or recurrent hydrocephalus 5.9 years after surgery, whereas the second patient maintained independent daily functioning without evidence of tumor progression at 8 months postoperatively. Conclusion Surgical resection with intraoperative facial nerve monitoring may provide favorable functional and radiological outcomes in carefully selected octogenarians with large VSs associated with hydrocephalus.

title: Rapid enlargement of a cervicomedullary junction neurenteric cyst with de novo fluid-fluid level formation.
abstract: Background Neurenteric cysts are rare congenital lesions that usually follow an indolent course. In cystic lesions, a fluid-fluid level generally indicates hemorrhage; in neurenteric cysts, it is seldom reported and poorly understood. Prior explanations rested largely on imaging and intraoperative inference. We report a cervicomedullary junction neurenteric cyst that enlarged rapidly after indolent growth, with a de novo fluid-fluid level in the absence of hemorrhage, and propose a histopathologically supported mechanism. Case description A 52-year-old man presented with posterior neck pain and dizziness. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a 22-mm cystic lesion. Imaging 17 years earlier showed a 14-mm lesion. Over the next month, the cyst enlarged to 26 mm, developing a de novo fluid-fluid level and perilesional edema. Although suspected, hemorrhage was not confirmed at surgery or on histopathology; the cyst contained viscous proteinaceous fluid. The resected cyst wall showed foam cell clusters, interpreted as indirect evidence of prior wall disruption. Complete resection was achieved without neurological deterioration or recurrence at 8 months. Conclusion A fluid-fluid level in a neurenteric cyst does not necessarily indicate hemorrhage. It may instead reflect a rise in intracystic pressure from chronic mucin secretion that progressively compromises the cyst wall, allowing osmotic influx of cerebrospinal fluid that drives rapid enlargement and dilutes the upper layer. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report in which foam cell clusters provide histological support for such a non-hemorrhagic mechanism in a neurenteric cyst. Interval growth or perilesional edema may precede deterioration and should prompt consideration of timely intervention.

title: Intraoperative motor-evoked potential monitoring during coil embolization of internal carotid-anterior choroidal artery aneurysms: A comparative case series and lessons on monitoring pitfalls.
abstract: Background Ischemic injury to the anterior choroidal artery (AChA) territory during coil embolization of internal carotid artery-AChA (ICA-AChA) aneurysms can be functionally devastating and is not always detected by angiography. We examined the utility and the interpretive pitfalls of intraoperative motor-evoked potential (MEP) monitoring in this specific aneurysm subgroup. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 16 consecutive patients who underwent coil embolization for ICA-AChA aneurysms at a single institution. Seven patients (2013-2025) were monitored with intraoperative MEP (MEP group); 9 patients (2005-2015) treated before monitoring was introduced served as a historical comparison group (non-MEP group). Angiographic AChA changes, MEP waveform changes, intraoperative interventions, and postoperative diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging were analyzed. Results Significant MEP amplitude reduction (≥50%) occurred in two monitored patients, prompting coil retrieval, microcatheter repositioning, or a procedural pause; amplitudes recovered in all. One patient showed transient MEP reduction without angiographic change (possible false-positive). No patient in the MEP group developed postoperative infarction (0%), whereas two of nine non-MEP patients did (22%). Conclusion In this small comparative series, MEP monitoring provided functional information complementary to angiography, with no infarctions in the monitored group. MEP changes must be interpreted alongside angiographic and clinical findings, as both false-positive and false-negative results occur. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective validation.

title: Microsurgical resection of a pure third ventricular craniopharyngioma through an interhemispheric transcallosal transforaminal approach.
abstract: Background Craniopharyngiomas account for approximately 2-4% of all intracranial tumors and demonstrate a bimodal age distribution, typically affecting children aged 5-9 years and adults aged 55-69 years. Third ventricular craniopharyngiomas are rare, benign epithelial tumors that may arise primarily within the third ventricle or secondarily extend from the suprasellar region; the purely intraventricular subtype is particularly rare, with a reported incidence ranging from 0.5% to 14% of all cases. Despite benign histology, infiltration of adjacent neural tissue imparts clinically aggressive behavior and complicates complete resection. Their deep location near the hypothalamus, optic apparatus, and fornices poses major surgical challenges, and transcallosal approaches risk cognitive or memory deficit. A purely third ventricular craniopharyngioma, classified as Type D by Yaşargil and Type IV by Kassam, is confined to the third ventricle and is not accessible through an endonasal approach, making transcranial routes more suitable given the tumor's deep location and proximity to critical neurovascular structures, although select cases of successful endonasal resection have been reported. Case description We present a 34-year-old woman with galactorrhea and progressive weight gain over 6 months, together with intermittent diplopia and headaches. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a homogeneously contrast-enhancing mass occupying the third ventricle, measuring 3.0 × 2.9 × 2.3 cm, with preservation of the pituitary stalk and third ventricular floor, causing moderate obstructive hydrocephalus. An interhemispheric transcallosal transforaminal approach was performed, with the dural opening adjusted according to the drainage pattern of the bridging veins, a 1.5 cm callosotomy, and septal fenestration. Gross total resection was achieved with preservation of the pituitary stalk, and a third ventriculostomy was performed to allow cerebrospinal fluid flow. Postoperative magnetic resonance imaging confirmed complete resection, and histopathological examination confirmed a World Health Organization Grade I papillary craniopharyngioma. Surveillance imaging at 27 months confirmed tumor recurrence, and the patient was referred for radiation therapy, after which no further recurrence was observed. Follow-up imaging at 48 months demonstrated continued absence of disease. Conclusion Although there are reports of purely intraventricular craniopharyngiomas resected through the endonasal route, traditional transcranial approaches remain the standard for tumors located entirely within the third ventricle. Although this case was treated before routine molecular testing and targeted therapy became standard, modern management now requires a multidisciplinary strategy integrating microsurgery, radiotherapy, and targeted therapy with BRAF (B-Raf proto-oncogene, serine/threonine kinase) and MEK (mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase) inhibitors when appropriate.

title: Challenges in diagnosis and management of traumatic diaphragmatic injuries: experiences from a regional New Zealand trauma centre.
abstract: Background Diaphragmatic injury is a rare but serious consequence of thoraco-abdominal trauma, often overlooked due to its subtle initial presentation. Early recognition and surgical intervention of traumatic diaphragmatic injury (TDI) are paramount to treat life-threatening injuries, yet the diagnosis remains challenging due to the non-specific nature of symptoms and the limitations of conventional imaging techniques. This study aims to examine the burden of TDI among trauma patients of all injury severities presenting to the Level 1 trauma centre in New Zealand and evaluate the utility of pre-operative imaging in detecting patients who require operative repair of TDI. Method A retrospective review of the Te Manawa Taki (TMT) Region's trauma registry from 2014 to 2023, with TDIs identified using Abbreviated Injury Scale diagnosis codes 440602, 440604, 440606, 440608, 440610 and 440699, was conducted. This is complemented by a review of clinical records of TDI patients admitted to the Level 1 trauma centre in the TMT Region to evaluate pre-operative imaging techniques used. Results The diagnosis of TDI was made pre-operatively in 29 of 43 patients (67.4%). The injury was visible on chest X-ray (CXR) in 19 patients (44%) and on computed tomography (CT) alone in 26 patients (81%). In 14 patients (32.5%) the diagnosis was only made intraoperatively. The detection rate of radiological imaging is significantly lower than intraoperative detection (rate ratios for CXR and CT are 0.44 and 0.81, respectively; p<0.05). Conclusion TDI remains a rare and challenging diagnosis to establish solely through radiological imaging. Since TDI is often linked with other injuries, a low threshold for surgical intervention could be considered.

title: Prognostic value of the Epidural Spinal Cord Compression scale, Revised Tokuhashi, and Spine Instability Neoplastic Scores in primary stereotactic body radiotherapy for spinal bone metastases.
abstract: Objective Stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) has emerged as a highly effective, noninvasive treatment for spinal bone metastases (SBMs). However, long-term outcomes of primary SBRT and the comparative prognostic performance of commonly used decision-making tools remain incompletely defined. This study evaluated long-term local control (LC) and systematically compared the predictive value of the Epidural Spinal Cord Compression (ESCC) grade, Spine Instability Neoplastic Score (SINS), and revised Tokuhashi score (rTS). Methods The authors retrospectively analyzed 330 patients with 537 SBMs treated with primary CyberKnife SBRT between 2012 and 2023. SBMs with surgical indications under the NOMS (neurological, oncological, mechanical, and systemic) framework, defined as high-grade epidural compression (ESCC grade 2 or 3) and/or spinal instability (SINS > 12), were excluded. LC was defined as absence of radiographic tumor regrowth ≥ 6 months post-SBRT. Cox proportional hazards models identified independent predictors of local progression (LP). Prognostic discrimination of the ESCC grade, SINS, rTS, and a novel integrated multivariable model was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results The 1- and 2-year LC rates were 86.2% and 75.9%, respectively, with a median time to LP of 12 months. Independent predictors of LP included radioresistant histology, epidural compression, pain, osteolytic destruction, single-fraction equivalent dose < 20 Gy, and repeat SBRT. Even minimal epidural compression was strongly associated with inferior LC (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 2.01, p < 0.001). SBMs with SINS 7-12 also demonstrated significantly worse LC compared with SINS < 7 (aHR 1.78, p = 0.002). The prognostic contribution of rTS was largely driven by performance status alone. ROC analysis showed that the integrated model consistently outperformed the ESCC grade, SINS, and rTS at 1, 3, and 5 years (area under the curve 0.72-0.75 vs 0.59-0.65, all p < 0.05). Acute adverse events occurred in 33.9% of treated SBMs, predominantly pain flare (14.2%). Vertebral fractures developed in 17.0%, 24.2% of which were associated with LP. Conclusions Primary SBRT for SBMs provided durable LC with acceptable toxicity. Although the ESCC grade, SINS, and rTS offered moderate prognostic utility, an integrated multivariable model incorporating tumor, anatomical, and clinical factors demonstrated superior predictive accuracy. Comprehensive risk stratification may refine patient selection and optimize SBRT strategies.

title: Beyond TMJ pain: resolution of diffuse cervicobrachialgia after excision of a TMJ synovial cyst. An atypical case report.
abstract: Synovial cysts of the temporomandibular joint are rare, typically manifesting with local symptoms such as preauricular pain and swelling; magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for diagnosis. A 45-year-old woman presented with left preauricular pain, limited mouth opening (maximum interincisal distance of approximately 24 mm), and chronic diffuse cervicobrachialgia radiating from the neck to the fingertips. MRI revealed a 6.2-mm cystic lesion at the posteromedial aspect of the left TMJ, associated with disc displacement. Surgical excision via a preauricular approach resulted in complete removal of the cyst, which was confirmed by postoperative computed tomography (CT). Cervicobrachialgia resolved within one week postoperatively. The patient also experienced transient facial paresthesia, which completely subsided within one month. These findings, together with the known overlap between TMJ and cervical innervation, suggest that TMJ synovial cyst excision may alleviate both local and referred distant pain. For general dentists, persistent preauricular pain associated with limited mandibular opening and atypical cervicobrachial symptoms should raise suspicion of intra-articular TMJ pathology when routine dental and musculoskeletal evaluations are inconclusive. Early recognition and referral for MRI assessment may facilitate definitive diagnosis and appropriate management.
